new_sources.summary: # The Trinitarian Framework of the Nicene Creed. Editor’s Note: What follows is a chapter from *The Nicene Creed*, edited by Leonardo de Chirico and Mark Gilbert, published by and available from Matthias Media. > *We believe in one God,*. > *And in one Lord Jesus Christ,*. > *And we believe in the Holy Spirit,*. The Nicene Creed is built on the confession of God as one in nature and three in persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Motivated to clarify the identity of Jesus Christ as the Son of God incarnate, the Council of Nicaea framed its recognition of Jesus Christ as having the same nature as the Father in the context of God as Trinity.

This doctrine, which says that each person of the Trinity acts inseparably with the others in every act of God with respect to things outside Himself, helps us understand that each person is involved in everything God does in a manner that is appropriate to that person. Every action of God is from the Father through the Son and in the Holy Spirit, and this is an order that is inherent to God's triune identity. We have seen the doctrine of inseparable operations in both creation and atonement, and today we will look at the doctrine as it is revealed in the work of redemption more generally. new_sources.summary: The Hair Dreadlocks Ruwatan Ritual in the Dieng Plateau, particularly in Dieng Kulon Village, is a sacred tradition of Javanese society that represents a complex relationship between spirituality, local cosmology, ritual arts, and social structure. Dreadlocked hair is not understood merely as a biological phenomenon, but as a symbol of an individual’s connection with ancestors and supernatural forces, thus requiring a ruwatan ritual to restore physical, emotional, and spiritual balance.
